name: John McGee
role: Contractor who built the Medora slaughter-house
bio: John McGee was foreman of a carpenter crew in December 1884 and the contractor who finished the slaughter-house in 1885, a building the paper called equal to any of its kind in the United States. In January 1885 he was thinking of settling in Medora to build, and in September he left for Jamestown after the finishing touches.

moments.label: Left for Jamestown after completing the slaughter-house

John McGee took advantage of the severe weather of last week to make a business trip to Jamestown. He is thinking of taking up his residence here and engaging in building.
John O'Sullivan has presented contractor McGee with a fine bird dog.
Contractor McGee finishes the work on the slaughter-house to-day. The building is pronounced by those who should know as equal to any building of its kind in the United States.
